- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.

- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.

- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.

- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

input.fullContext:
You are in a benchmark workspace containing a Rust reference application at ./rust-reference and an official reference CLI path recorded in ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

input.fullContext:
You are in a benchmark workspace containing a Rust reference application at ./rust-reference and an official reference CLI path recorded in ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

+def _missing_value(spec: ArgSpec, flag: str) -> CliError:

+def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str]) -> ParsedArgs:
+    result = ParsedArgs()
+    index = 0
+    options_finished = False
+    while index < len(argv):
+        token = argv[index]
+        if options_finished or token == "-" or not token.startswith("-"):
+            result.paths.append(token)
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        if token == "--":
+            options_finished = True
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("--"):
+            body = token[2:]
+            name, equal, attached = body.partition("=")
+            spec = LONG_SPECS.get(name)
+            if spec is None:
+                raise CliError(f"Unknown argument --{name}")
+            flag = f"--{name}"
+            value: Optional[str] = None
+            if spec.value_kind == "none":
+                if equal:
+                    raise CliError(f"Flag {flag} cannot take a value")
+            elif spec.value_kind == "required":
+                if equal:
+                    value = attached
+                elif index + 1 < len(argv):
+                    index += 1
+                    value = argv[index]
+                else:
+                    raise _missing_value(spec, flag)
+            else:

+                elif index + 1 < len(argv) and argv[index + 1] in spec.choices:
+                    index += 1
+                    value = argv[index]
+                else:
+                    value = spec.default
+            result.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, flag, value))
+            index += 1
+            continue
+
+        body = token[1:]
+        offset = 0
+        while offset < len(body):
+            short = body[offset]
+            spec = SHORT_SPECS.get(short)
+            if spec is None:
+                raise CliError(f"Unknown argument -{short}")
+            flag = f"-{short}"
+            value = None
+            remainder = body[offset + 1:]
+            if spec.value_kind == "none":
+                if remainder.startswith("="):
+                    raise CliError(f"Flag {flag} cannot take a value")
+                result.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, flag))
+                offset += 1
+                continue
+            if remainder:
+                value = remainder[1:] if remainder.startswith("=") else remainder
+                offset = len(body)
+            elif spec.value_kind == "required":
+                if index + 1 >= len(argv):

+                index += 1
+                value = argv[index]
+                offset = len(body)
+            elif index + 1 < len(argv) and argv[index + 1] in spec.choices:

+                value = argv[index]
+                offset = len(body)
+            else:
+                value = spec.default
+                offset = len(body)
+            result.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, flag, value))
+        index += 1

+def rust_debug(value: str) -> str:
+    escaped: list[str] = []
+    for char in value:
+        code = ord(char)
+        if char == "\\":
+            escaped.append("\\\\")
+        elif char == '"':
+            escaped.append('\\"')
+        elif char == "\n":
+            escaped.append("\\n")
+        elif char == "\r":
+            escaped.append("\\r")
+        elif char == "\t":
+            escaped.append("\\t")
+        elif code < 32 or code == 127:
+            escaped.append(f"\\u{{{code:x}}}")
+        else:
+            escaped.append(char)
+    return '"' + "".join(escaped) + '"'
+

+    return CliError(

+    )

+def parse_usize(value: str, source: str) -> int:
+    if not value or value.startswith("-") or not value.isdecimal():
+        reason = "invalid digit found in string"
+        raise CliError(f"Value {rust_debug(value)} not valid for {source}: {reason}")
+    number = int(value, 10)
+    if number > (1 << 64) - 1:
+        reason = "number too large to fit in target type"
+        raise CliError(f"Value {rust_debug(value)} not valid for {source}: {reason}")
+    return number

+def _validate_when(parsed: ParsedArgs, names: Sequence[str]) -> Optional[str]:
+    item = parsed.last(*names)
+    if item is None:
+        return None
+    assert item.value is not None
+    if item.value not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+        raise bad_setting(item.spec, item.value, False)
+    return item.value
+

+def deduce_options(parsed: ParsedArgs) -> Options:
+    _validate_when(parsed, ("color", "colour"))
+    _validate_when(parsed, ("icons",))
+    classify = _validate_when(parsed, ("classify",)) or "never"
+
+    sort_item = parsed.last("sort")
+    sort_word = sort_item.value if sort_item is not None else "name"
+    assert sort_word is not None
+    if sort_word not in SORT_ALIASES:
+        assert sort_item is not None
+        raise bad_setting(sort_item.spec, sort_word, True)
+    sort_field = SORT_ALIASES[sort_word]
+
+    width_item = parsed.last("width")
+    width: Optional[int] = None
+    if width_item is not None:
+        assert width_item.value is not None
+        width = parse_usize(width_item.value, "option --width (-w)")
+    elif os.environ.get("COLUMNS"):
+        width = parse_usize(os.environ["COLUMNS"], "environment variable COLUMNS")
+
+    max_level = None
+    level_item = parsed.last("level")
+    if level_item is not None:
+        assert level_item.value is not None
+        max_level = parse_usize(level_item.value, "option --level (-L)")
+
+    all_count = parsed.count("all")
+    show_hidden = all_count > 0 or parsed.has("almost-all")
+    show_dots = all_count >= 2
+    if show_dots and parsed.has("tree"):
+        raise CliError("Option --tree is useless given --all --all")
+
+    mode_flag = parsed.last("long", "oneline", "grid", "tree")
+    long_present = parsed.has("long")
+    stdout_tty = bool(getattr(sys.stdout, "isatty", lambda: False)())
+    terminal_known = width is not None or stdout_tty
+    if mode_flag is None:
+        mode = "grid" if terminal_known else "lines"
+        metadata = False
+    elif mode_flag.spec.name == "oneline":
+        mode = "lines"
+        metadata = False
+    elif (
+        mode_flag.spec.name == "long"
+        or (mode_flag.spec.name in ("tree", "grid") and long_present)
+    ):
+        tree_or_grid = parsed.last("tree", "grid")
+        mode = "grid_details" if tree_or_grid and tree_or_grid.spec.name == "grid" else "details"
+        metadata = True
+    elif mode_flag.spec.name == "tree":
+        mode = "details"
+        metadata = False
+    else:
+        mode = "grid"
+        metadata = False
+

+    recurse = not tree and parsed.has("recurse")
+    as_file = not tree and not recurse and (
+        parsed.has("treat-dirs-as-files") or parsed.has("list-dirs")
+    )
+
+    absolute_item = parsed.last("absolute")
+    absolute = absolute_item.value if absolute_item is not None else "off"
+    assert absolute is not None
+    absolute_aliases = {"on": "on", "yes": "on", "follow": "follow", "off": "off", "no": "off"}
+    if absolute not in absolute_aliases:
+        assert absolute_item is not None
+        raise bad_setting(absolute_item.spec, absolute, False)
+    absolute = absolute_aliases[absolute]
+
+    size_item = parsed.last("binary", "bytes")
+    size_format = "decimal"
+    if size_item is not None:
+        size_format = "binary" if size_item.spec.name == "binary" else "bytes"
+
+    time_item = parsed.last("time", "modified", "accessed", "created", "changed")
+    time_field = "modified"
+    if time_item is not None:
+        if time_item.spec.name == "time":
+            assert time_item.value is not None
+            if time_item.value not in TIME_CHOICES:
+                raise bad_setting(time_item.spec, time_item.value, True)
+            time_field = time_item.value
+        else:
+            time_field = time_item.spec.name
+
+    time_style_item = parsed.last("time-style")
+    time_style = os.environ.get("TIME_STYLE", "default")
+    if time_style_item is not None:
+        assert time_style_item.value is not None
+        time_style = time_style_item.value
+    if time_style not in TIME_STYLE_CHOICES and not time_style.startswith("+"):
+        spec = LONG_SPECS["time-style"]
+        raise bad_setting(spec, time_style, False)
+
+    ignore_item = parsed.last("ignore-glob")
+    ignore_patterns = ignore_item.value.split("|") if ignore_item and ignore_item.value else []
+
+    return Options(
+        mode=mode, metadata=metadata, tree=tree, recurse=recurse, as_file=as_file,
+        max_level=max_level, width=width, across=parsed.has("across"),
+        show_hidden=show_hidden, show_dots=show_dots,
+        reverse=parsed.has("reverse"), sort_field=sort_field,
+        dirs_first=parsed.has("group-directories-first"),
+        dirs_last=parsed.has("group-directories-last"),
+        only_dirs=parsed.has("only-dirs"), only_files=parsed.has("only-files"),
+        no_symlinks=parsed.has("no-symlinks"),
+        show_symlinks=parsed.has("show-symlinks"),
+        ignore_patterns=ignore_patterns, classify=classify,
+        quote_spaces=not parsed.has("no-quotes"), absolute=absolute,
+        dereference=parsed.has("dereference"),
+        follow_symlinks=parsed.has("follow-symlinks"),
+        size_format=size_format, header=parsed.has("header"),
+        no_permissions=parsed.has("no-permissions"),
+        no_filesize=parsed.has("no-filesize"), no_time=parsed.has("no-time"),
+        time_field=time_field, time_style=time_style, stdin=parsed.has("stdin"),
+        stdout_tty=stdout_tty,
+    )

+def display_width(text: str) -> int:
+    width = 0
+    for char in text:
+        if unicodedata.combining(char):
+            continue
+        width += 2 if unicodedata.east_asian_width(char) in ("W", "F") else 1
+    return width
+
+
+def pad(text: str, width: int, right: bool = False) -> str:
+    count = max(0, width - display_width(text))
+    return (" " * count + text) if right else (text + " " * count)
+
+
+def normalize_input_display(raw: str) -> str:
+    if raw in (".", ".."):
+        return raw
+    trimmed = raw.rstrip("\\/")
+    if not trimmed:
+        return raw
+    parent = os.path.dirname(trimmed)
+    name = os.path.basename(trimmed)
+    return os.path.join(parent, name) if parent else name

+@dataclass
+class Entry:
+    path: str
+    name: str
+    display: str
+    explicit: bool = False
+    synthetic: bool = False
+    _lstat: Optional[os.stat_result] = field(default=None, repr=False)
+
+    def lstat(self) -> os.stat_result:
+        if self._lstat is None:
+            self._lstat = os.lstat(self.path)
+        return self._lstat
+
+    def metadata(self, dereference: bool = False) -> os.stat_result:
+        return os.stat(self.path) if dereference else self.lstat()
+
+    def is_link(self) -> bool:
+        if self.synthetic:
+            return False
+        try:
+            return _stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def is_dir(self, follow: bool = False) -> bool:
+        if self.synthetic:
+            return True
+        try:
+            if self.is_link() and not follow:
+                return False
+            return _stat.S_ISDIR(self.metadata(follow).st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def attributes(self) -> int:
+        try:
+            return int(getattr(self.lstat(), "st_file_attributes", 0))
+        except OSError:
+            return 0
+
+    def is_hidden(self) -> bool:
+        hidden_bit = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN", 0x2))
+        return self.name.startswith(".") or bool(self.attributes() & hidden_bit)
+

+def make_explicit(raw: str, options: Options) -> Entry:
+    if options.absolute == "follow":
+        display = os.path.realpath(raw)
+    elif options.absolute == "on":
+        display = os.path.abspath(raw)
+    else:
+        display = normalize_input_display(raw)
+    trimmed = raw.rstrip("\\/") or raw
+    name = os.path.basename(trimmed) or raw
+    return Entry(raw, name, display, explicit=True)
+
+
+def make_child(directory: str, name: str, options: Options) -> Entry:
+    path = os.path.join(directory, name)
+    if options.absolute == "follow":
+        display = os.path.realpath(path)
+    elif options.absolute == "on":
+        display = os.path.abspath(path)
+    else:
+        display = name
+    return Entry(path, name, display)
+
+
+def _natural_parts(text: str, ignore_case: bool) -> list[tuple[int, object, int]]:
+    source = text.lower() if ignore_case else text
+    result: list[tuple[int, object, int]] = []
+    for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", source):
+        if part.isdigit():
+            result.append((1, int(part), -len(part)))
+        else:
+            result.append((0, part, 0))
+    return result
+
+
+def natural_compare(left: str, right: str, ignore_case: bool = True) -> int:
+    lparts = _natural_parts(left, ignore_case)
+    rparts = _natural_parts(right, ignore_case)
+    for lpart, rpart in zip(lparts, rparts):
+        if lpart < rpart:
+            return -1
+        if lpart > rpart:
+            return 1
+    return (len(lparts) > len(rparts)) - (len(lparts) < len(rparts))
+
+
+def extension_of(name: str) -> str:
+    if name.startswith(".") and name.count(".") == 1:
+        return ""
+    if "." not in name:
+        return ""
+    return name.rsplit(".", 1)[1]
+
+
+def entry_timestamp_ns(entry: Entry, field_name: str) -> int:
+    try:
+        info = entry.lstat()
+    except OSError:
+        return 0
+    if field_name == "accessed":
+        return int(getattr(info, "st_atime_ns", int(info.st_atime * 1_000_000_000)))
+    if field_name == "created":
+        if hasattr(info, "st_birthtime_ns"):
+            return int(info.st_birthtime_ns)
+        if hasattr(info, "st_birthtime"):
+            return int(info.st_birthtime * 1_000_000_000)
+        return int(getattr(info, "st_ctime_ns", int(info.st_ctime * 1_000_000_000)))
+    if field_name == "changed":
+        return int(getattr(info, "st_ctime_ns", int(info.st_ctime * 1_000_000_000)))
+    return int(getattr(info, "st_mtime_ns", int(info.st_mtime * 1_000_000_000)))
+
+
+def entry_size(entry: Entry) -> int:
+    try:
+        return int(entry.lstat().st_size)
+    except OSError:
+        return 0
+
+
+def entry_kind(entry: Entry) -> int:
+    try:
+        mode = entry.lstat().st_mode
+    except OSError:
+        return 7
+    if _stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
+        return 0
+    if _stat.S_ISREG(mode):
+        return 1
+    if _stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
+        return 2
+    if _stat.S_ISFIFO(mode):
+        return 3
+    if _stat.S_ISSOCK(mode):
+        return 4
+    if _stat.S_ISCHR(mode):
+        return 5
+    if _stat.S_ISBLK(mode):
+        return 6
+    return 7
+
+
+def compare_entries(left: Entry, right: Entry, options: Options) -> int:
+    left_dir = left.is_dir(False)
+    right_dir = right.is_dir(False)
+    if left_dir != right_dir:
+        if options.dirs_first:
+            return -1 if left_dir else 1
+        if options.dirs_last:
+            return 1 if left_dir else -1
+
+    field_name = options.sort_field
+    comparison = 0
+    if field_name in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name"):
+        mix_hidden = field_name.startswith(".")
+        case_sensitive = field_name.endswith("Name")
+        if not mix_hidden and left.is_hidden() != right.is_hidden():
+            comparison = -1 if left.is_hidden() else 1
+        else:
+            lname = left.name.lstrip(".") if mix_hidden else left.name
+            rname = right.name.lstrip(".") if mix_hidden else right.name
+            comparison = natural_compare(lname, rname, not case_sensitive)
+    elif field_name in ("extension", "Extension"):
+        lext, rext = extension_of(left.name), extension_of(right.name)
+        if not lext and not rext and left.is_hidden() != right.is_hidden():
+            comparison = 1 if left.is_hidden() else -1
+        else:
+            comparison = natural_compare(lext, rext, field_name == "extension")
+        if comparison == 0:
+            comparison = natural_compare(left.name, right.name, field_name == "extension")
+    elif field_name == "size":
+        comparison = (entry_size(left) > entry_size(right)) - (entry_size(left) < entry_size(right))
+    elif field_name in ("modified", "age", "accessed", "created", "changed"):
+        actual_field = "modified" if field_name == "age" else field_name
+        ltime = entry_timestamp_ns(left, actual_field)
+        rtime = entry_timestamp_ns(right, actual_field)
+        comparison = (ltime > rtime) - (ltime < rtime)
+        if field_name == "age":
+            comparison *= -1
+    elif field_name == "inode":
+        lino = int(getattr(left.lstat(), "st_ino", 0))
+        rino = int(getattr(right.lstat(), "st_ino", 0))
+        comparison = (lino > rino) - (lino < rino)
+    elif field_name == "type":
+        comparison = (entry_kind(left) > entry_kind(right)) - (entry_kind(left) < entry_kind(right))
+    elif field_name == "none":
+        comparison = 0
+
+    if comparison == 0 and field_name not in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name", "none"):
+        comparison = natural_compare(left.name, right.name, True)
+    return -comparison if options.reverse else comparison
+
+
+def sort_entries(entries: Iterable[Entry], options: Options) -> list[Entry]:
+    values = list(entries)
+    if options.sort_field == "none":
+        if options.reverse:
+            values.reverse()
+        return values
+    values.sort(key=cmp_to_key(lambda a, b: compare_entries(a, b, options)))
+    return values
+
+
+def visible_base(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> bool:
+    if not options.show_hidden and entry.is_hidden():
+        return False
+    if options.no_symlinks and entry.is_link():
+        return False
+    if any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(entry.name, pattern) for pattern in options.ignore_patterns):
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def display_filter(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> bool:
+    if options.only_dirs and options.only_files:
+        return entry.is_link() and options.show_symlinks
+    if entry.is_link() and options.show_symlinks:
+        return True
+    if options.only_dirs:
+        return entry.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks)
+    if options.only_files:
+        return not entry.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks) and not entry.is_link()
+    return True
+
+
+def scan_directory(directory: str, options: Options) -> tuple[list[Entry], Optional[OSError]]:
+    entries: list[Entry] = []
+    try:
+        with os.scandir(directory) as iterator:
+            for item in iterator:
+                entry = make_child(directory, item.name, options)
+                try:
+                    entry._lstat = item.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
+                except OSError:
+                    pass
+                if visible_base(entry, options):
+                    entries.append(entry)
+    except OSError as error:
+        return [], error
+    if options.show_dots and not options.tree:
+        entries.extend([
+            Entry(directory, ".", ".", synthetic=True),
+            Entry(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(directory)), "..", "..", synthetic=True),
+        ])
+    return sort_entries(entries, options), None
+
+
+def quote_name(text: str, enabled: bool) -> str:
+    return f"'{text}'" if enabled and " " in text else text
+
+
+def classify_suffix(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> str:
+    enabled = options.classify == "always" or (
+        options.classify in ("auto", "automatic") and options.stdout_tty
+    )
+    if not enabled:
+        return ""
+    if entry.is_link():
+        return "@"
+    if entry.is_dir(False):
+        return "/"
+    try:
+        mode = entry.lstat().st_mode
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+    if _stat.S_ISFIFO(mode):
+        return "|"
+    if _stat.S_ISSOCK(mode):
+        return "="
+    if os.name != "nt" and _stat.S_ISREG(mode) and mode & 0o111:
+        return "*"
+    return ""
+
+
+def render_name(entry: Entry, options: Options, override: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+    base = override if override is not None else entry.display
+    base = quote_name(base + classify_suffix(entry, options), options.quote_spaces)
+    if entry.is_link():
+        try:
+            target = os.readlink(entry.path)
+        except OSError:
+            target = None
+        if target is not None:
+            base += " -> " + quote_name(target, options.quote_spaces)
+    return base
+
+
+def format_size(number: int, style: str) -> str:
+    if style == "bytes":
+        return f"{number:,}"
+    if style == "binary":
+        base, suffixes = 1024, ("", "Ki", "Mi", "Gi", "Ti", "Pi", "Ei")
+    else:
+        base, suffixes = 1000, ("", "k", "M", "G", "T", "P", "E")
+    unit = 0
+    scale = float(number)
+    while number >= base ** (unit + 1) and unit + 1 < len(suffixes):
+        unit += 1
+        scale = number / float(base ** unit)
+    if unit == 0:
+        return f"{number:,}"
+    if scale < 10:
+        rendered = f"{scale:.1f}"
+    else:
+        rendered = f"{scale:,.0f}"
+    return rendered + suffixes[unit]
+
+
+def windows_mode(entry: Entry) -> str:
+    attrs = entry.attributes()
+    archive = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE", 0x20))
+    readonly = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY", 0x1))
+    hidden = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN", 0x2))
+    system = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM", 0x4))
+    kind = "l" if entry.is_link() else ("d" if entry.is_dir(False) else "-")
+    return "".join((
+        kind,
+        "a" if attrs & archive and kind != "d" else "-",
+        "r" if attrs & readonly else "-",
+        "h" if attrs & hidden else "-",
+        "s" if attrs & system else "-",
+    ))
+
+
+def mode_text(entry: Entry) -> str:
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        return windows_mode(entry)
+    try:
+        return _stat.filemode(entry.lstat().st_mode)
+    except OSError:
+        return "??????????"
+
+
+MONTHS = ("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")
+
+
+def datetime_for_ns(value: int) -> _datetime.datetime:
+    seconds, _ = divmod(value, 1_000_000_000)
+    return _datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(seconds, _datetime.timezone.utc).astimezone()
+
+
+def custom_time_format(moment: _datetime.datetime, pattern: str) -> str:
+    marker = "__EZA_SPACE_DAY__"
+    pattern = pattern.replace("%_d", marker)
+    try:
+        rendered = moment.strftime(pattern)
+    except (ValueError, OSError):
+        rendered = pattern
+    return rendered.replace(marker, f"{moment.day:2d}")
+
+
+def format_time(value: int, style: str) -> str:
+    moment = datetime_for_ns(value)
+    if style == "long-iso":
+        return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
+    if style == "full-iso":
+        nanos = value % 1_000_000_000
+        return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.") + f"{nanos:09d} " + moment.strftime("%z")
+    if style == "iso":
+        if moment.year == _datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().year:
+            return moment.strftime("%m-%d %H:%M")
+        return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
+    if style == "relative":
+        seconds = int((_datetime.datetime.now().astimezone() - moment).total_seconds())
+        future = seconds < 0
+        amount = abs(seconds)
+        if amount < 60:
+            return "now"
+        units = ((31_536_000, "year"), (2_592_000, "month"), (86_400, "day"),
+                 (3_600, "hour"), (60, "minute"))
+        for span, label in units:
+            if amount >= span:
+                count = amount // span
+                word = label if count == 1 else label + "s"
+                return f"in {count} {word}" if future else f"{count} {word} ago"
+    if style.startswith("+"):
+        pattern = style[1:].split("\n", 1)[0]
+        return custom_time_format(moment, pattern)
+    current_year = _datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().year
+    if moment.year == current_year:
+        return f"{moment.day:2d} {MONTHS[moment.month - 1]} {moment:%H:%M}"
+    return f"{moment.day:2d} {MONTHS[moment.month - 1]}  {moment.year:04d}"
+
+
+def long_cells(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    cells: list[str] = []
+    if not options.no_permissions:
+        cells.append(mode_text(entry))
+    if not options.no_filesize:
+        if entry.is_dir(False):
+            cells.append("-")
+        else:
+            try:
+                cells.append(format_size(int(entry.metadata(options.dereference).st_size), options.size_format))
+            except OSError:
+                cells.append("-")
+    if not options.no_time:
+        cells.append(format_time(entry_timestamp_ns(entry, options.time_field), options.time_style))
+    return cells
+
+
+def column_headers(options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    headers: list[str] = []
+    if not options.no_permissions:
+        headers.append("Mode" if os.name == "nt" else "Permissions")
+    if not options.no_filesize:
+        headers.append("Size")
+    if not options.no_time:
+        names = {"modified": "Modified", "accessed": "Accessed", "created": "Created", "changed": "Changed"}
+        headers.append("Date " + names[options.time_field])
+    return headers
+
+
+def render_long(
+    entries: Sequence[Entry], options: Options,
+    name_overrides: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
+) -> list[str]:
+    rows = [long_cells(entry, options) for entry in entries]
+    headers = column_headers(options)
+    widths: list[int] = []
+    for index in range(len(headers)):
+        values = [headers[index]] if options.header else []
+        values.extend(row[index] for row in rows)
+        widths.append(max((display_width(value) for value in values), default=0))
+
+    lines: list[str] = []
+    if options.header:
+        formatted = []
+        for index, text in enumerate(headers):
+            right = index != 0 or options.no_permissions
+            formatted.append(pad(text, widths[index], right))
+        prefix = " ".join(formatted)
+        lines.append((prefix + " " if prefix else "") + "Name")
+    for row_index, (entry, row) in enumerate(zip(entries, rows)):
+        formatted = []
+        for index, text in enumerate(row):
+            right = index != 0 or options.no_permissions
+            formatted.append(pad(text, widths[index], right))
+        prefix = " ".join(formatted)
+        override = name_overrides[row_index] if name_overrides is not None else None
+        name = render_name(entry, options, override)
+        lines.append((prefix + " " if prefix else "") + name)
+    return lines
+
+
+def render_grid(cells: Sequence[str], width: Optional[int], across: bool) -> list[str]:
+    if not cells or width is None or width <= 0:
+        return list(cells)
+    count = len(cells)
+    selected_columns = 1
+    selected_widths = [max(display_width(cell) for cell in cells)]
+    for columns in range(count, 0, -1):
+        rows = math.ceil(count / columns)
+        widths: list[int] = []
+        for column in range(columns):
+            if across:
+                indices = range(column, count, columns)
+            else:
+                start = column * rows
+                indices = range(start, min(start + rows, count))
+            values = [display_width(cells[i]) for i in indices]
+            widths.append(max(values, default=0))
+        if sum(widths) + 2 * (columns - 1) <= width:
+            selected_columns, selected_widths = columns, widths
+            break
+    rows = math.ceil(count / selected_columns)
+    lines: list[str] = []
+    for row in range(rows):
+        pieces: list[str] = []
+        for column in range(selected_columns):
+            index = row * selected_columns + column if across else column * rows + row
+            if index >= count:
+                continue
+            text = cells[index]
+            if column + 1 < selected_columns:
+                text = pad(text, selected_widths[column]) + "  "
+            pieces.append(text)
+        lines.append("".join(pieces).rstrip())
+    return lines
+
+
+def actual_width(options: Options) -> Optional[int]:
+    if options.width is not None:
+        return options.width
+    if options.stdout_tty:
+        return shutil.get_terminal_size(fallback=(80, 24)).columns
+    return None
+
+
+def render_block(entries: Sequence[Entry], options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    displayed = [entry for entry in entries if display_filter(entry, options)]
+    if options.mode == "details":
+        if options.metadata:
+            return render_long(displayed, options)
+        return [render_name(entry, options) for entry in displayed]
+    if options.mode == "grid_details":
+        detail_lines = render_long(displayed, options)
+        return render_grid(detail_lines, actual_width(options), options.across)
+    names = [render_name(entry, options) for entry in displayed]
+    if options.mode == "grid":
+        return render_grid(names, actual_width(options), options.across)
+    return names
+
+
+def os_error_number(error: OSError) -> int:
+    return int(getattr(error, "winerror", None) or getattr(error, "errno", None) or 1)
+
+
+def os_error_message(error: OSError) -> str:
+    number = os_error_number(error)
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        try:
+            message = ctypes.FormatError(number).strip()
+        except (ValueError, OSError):
+            message = ""
+    else:
+        try:
+            message = os.strerror(number)
+        except ValueError:
+            message = str(error)
+    message = message.rstrip("\r\n")
+    return f"{message} (os error {number})"
+

+@dataclass
+class DirectoryContext:
+    path: str
+    label: str
+
+
+def child_context(parent: DirectoryContext, entry: Entry) -> DirectoryContext:
+    return DirectoryContext(entry.path, os.path.join(parent.label, entry.name))
+
+
+def render_tree_root(root: Entry, options: Options, errors: list[str]) -> tuple[list[Entry], list[str]]:
+    entries: list[Entry] = [root]
+    names: list[str] = [root.display]
+
+    def descend(directory: Entry, ancestors: list[bool], depth: int) -> None:
+        if options.max_level is not None and depth >= options.max_level:
+            return
+        children, error = scan_directory(directory.path, options)
+        if error is not None:
+            errors.append(f"{directory.path}: {os_error_message(error)}")
+            return
+        visible = [child for child in children if display_filter(child, options)]
+        for index, child in enumerate(visible):
+            last = index == len(visible) - 1
+            prefix = "".join("    " if was_last else "\u2502   " for was_last in ancestors)
+            prefix += "\u2514\u2500\u2500 " if last else "\u251c\u2500\u2500 "
+            entries.append(child)
+            names.append(prefix + child.display)
+            if child.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks):
+                descend(child, ancestors + [last], depth + 1)
+
+    if root.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks):
+        descend(root, [], 0)
+    return entries, names
+
+
+def render_tree(roots: Sequence[Entry], options: Options, errors: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    all_entries: list[Entry] = []
+    all_names: list[str] = []
+    for root in roots:
+        entries, names = render_tree_root(root, options, errors)
+        all_entries.extend(entries)
+        all_names.extend(names)
+    if options.metadata:
+        return render_long(all_entries, options, all_names)
+    return [render_name(entry, options, name) for entry, name in zip(all_entries, all_names)]
+
+
+def read_input_paths(parsed: ParsedArgs, options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    if parsed.paths:
+        return list(parsed.paths)
+    stdin_tty = bool(getattr(sys.stdin, "isatty", lambda: False)())
+    if options.stdin or not stdin_tty:
+        data = sys.stdin.read()
+        separator = os.environ.get("EZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR", "\n")
+        if separator == "":
+            return [part for part in data if part]
+        return [part for part in data.split(separator) if part]
+    return ["."]
+
+
+def execute(parsed: ParsedArgs, options: Options) -> tuple[str, str, int]:
+    paths = read_input_paths(parsed, options)
+    stderr_lines: list[str] = []
+    status = 0
+    roots: list[Entry] = []
+    files: list[Entry] = []
+    directories: list[DirectoryContext] = []
+
+    for raw in paths:
+        entry = make_explicit(raw, options)
+        try:
+            entry._lstat = os.lstat(raw)
+        except OSError as error:
+            stderr_lines.append(f"{rust_debug(raw)}: {os_error_message(error)}")
+            status = 2
+            continue
+        if options.tree:
+            roots.append(entry)
+        elif entry.is_dir(False) and not options.as_file:
+            directories.append(DirectoryContext(raw, normalize_input_display(raw)))
+        else:
+            if visible_base(entry, options) and display_filter(entry, options):
+                files.append(entry)
+
+    if options.tree:
+        roots = sort_entries(roots, options)
+        lines = render_tree(roots, options, stderr_lines)
+        if stderr_lines:
+            status = 2
+        output = "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")
+        error_output = "\n".join(stderr_lines) + ("\n" if stderr_lines else "")
+        return output, error_output, status
+
+    files = sort_entries(files, options)
+    chunks: list[str] = []
+    if files:
+        chunks.append("\n".join(render_block(files, options)))
+
+    label_roots = len(directories) > 1 or bool(files)
+
+    def add_directory_block(context: DirectoryContext, labelled: bool) -> list[Entry]:
+        nonlocal status
+        entries, error = scan_directory(context.path, options)
+        if error is not None:
+            stderr_lines.append(f"{context.label}: {os_error_message(error)}")
+            status = 2
+            return []
+        lines = render_block(entries, options)
+        if labelled:
+            chunks.append(context.label + ":" + (("\n" + "\n".join(lines)) if lines else ""))
+        elif lines:
+            chunks.append("\n".join(lines))
+        return entries
+
+    def recurse_from(context: DirectoryContext, entries: Sequence[Entry], depth: int) -> None:
+        if options.max_level is not None and depth >= options.max_level:
+            return
+        for entry in entries:
+            if entry.synthetic or not entry.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks):
+                continue
+            child = child_context(context, entry)
+            child_entries = add_directory_block(child, True)
+            recurse_from(child, child_entries, depth + 1)
+
+    for context in directories:
+        entries = add_directory_block(context, label_roots)
+        if options.recurse:

+    def metadata(self, dereference: bool = False) -> os.stat_result:
+        return os.stat(self.path) if dereference else self.lstat()
+
+    def is_link(self) -> bool:
+        if self.synthetic:
+            return False
+        try:
+            return _stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def is_dir(self, follow: bool = False) -> bool:
+        if self.synthetic:
+            return True
+        try:
+            if self.is_link() and not follow:
+                return False
+            return _stat.S_ISDIR(self.metadata(follow).st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def attributes(self) -> int:
+        try:
+            return int(getattr(self.lstat(), "st_file_attributes", 0))
+        except OSError:
+            return 0
+
+    def is_hidden(self) -> bool:
+        hidden_bit = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN", 0x2))
+        return self.name.startswith(".") or bool(self.attributes() & hidden_bit)
+
+
+def make_explicit(raw: str, options: Options) -> Entry:
+    if options.absolute == "follow":
+        display = os.path.realpath(raw)
+    elif options.absolute == "on":
+        display = os.path.abspath(raw)
+    else:
+        display = normalize_input_display(raw)
+    trimmed = raw.rstrip("\\/") or raw
+    name = os.path.basename(trimmed) or raw
+    return Entry(raw, name, display, explicit=True)
+
+
+def make_child(directory: str, name: str, options: Options) -> Entry:
+    path = os.path.join(directory, name)
+    if options.absolute == "follow":
+        display = os.path.realpath(path)
+    elif options.absolute == "on":
+        display = os.path.abspath(path)
+    else:
+        display = name
+    return Entry(path, name, display)
+
+
+def _natural_parts(text: str, ignore_case: bool) -> list[tuple[int, object, int]]:
+    source = text.lower() if ignore_case else text
+    result: list[tuple[int, object, int]] = []
+    for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", source):
+        if part.isdigit():
+            result.append((1, int(part), -len(part)))
+        else:
+            result.append((0, part, 0))
+    return result
+
+
+def natural_compare(left: str, right: str, ignore_case: bool = True) -> int:
+    lparts = _natural_parts(left, ignore_case)
+    rparts = _natural_parts(right, ignore_case)
+    for lpart, rpart in zip(lparts, rparts):
+        if lpart < rpart:
+            return -1
+        if lpart > rpart:
+            return 1
+    return (len(lparts) > len(rparts)) - (len(lparts) < len(rparts))
+
+
+def extension_of(name: str) -> str:
+    if name.startswith(".") and name.count(".") == 1:
+        return ""
+    if "." not in name:
+        return ""
+    return name.rsplit(".", 1)[1]
+
+
+def entry_timestamp_ns(entry: Entry, field_name: str) -> int:
+    try:
+        info = entry.lstat()
+    except OSError:
+        return 0
+    if field_name == "accessed":
+        return int(getattr(info, "st_atime_ns", int(info.st_atime * 1_000_000_000)))
+    if field_name == "created":
+        if hasattr(info, "st_birthtime_ns"):
+            return int(info.st_birthtime_ns)
+        if hasattr(info, "st_birthtime"):
+            return int(info.st_birthtime * 1_000_000_000)
+        return int(getattr(info, "st_ctime_ns", int(info.st_ctime * 1_000_000_000)))
+    if field_name == "changed":
+        return int(getattr(info, "st_ctime_ns", int(info.st_ctime * 1_000_000_000)))
+    return int(getattr(info, "st_mtime_ns", int(info.st_mtime * 1_000_000_000)))
+
+
+def entry_size(entry: Entry) -> int:
+    try:
+        return int(entry.lstat().st_size)
+    except OSError:
+        return 0
+
+
+def entry_kind(entry: Entry) -> int:
+    try:
+        mode = entry.lstat().st_mode
+    except OSError:
+        return 7
+    if _stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
+        return 0
+    if _stat.S_ISREG(mode):
+        return 1
+    if _stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
+        return 2
+    if _stat.S_ISFIFO(mode):
+        return 3
+    if _stat.S_ISSOCK(mode):
+        return 4
+    if _stat.S_ISCHR(mode):
+        return 5
+    if _stat.S_ISBLK(mode):
+        return 6
+    return 7
+
+
+def compare_entries(left: Entry, right: Entry, options: Options) -> int:
+    left_dir = left.is_dir(False)
+    right_dir = right.is_dir(False)
+    if left_dir != right_dir:
+        if options.dirs_first:
+            return -1 if left_dir else 1
+        if options.dirs_last:
+            return 1 if left_dir else -1
+
+    field_name = options.sort_field
+    comparison = 0
+    if field_name in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name"):
+        mix_hidden = field_name.startswith(".")
+        case_sensitive = field_name.endswith("Name")
+        if not mix_hidden and left.is_hidden() != right.is_hidden():
+            comparison = -1 if left.is_hidden() else 1
+        else:
+            lname = left.name.lstrip(".") if mix_hidden else left.name
+            rname = right.name.lstrip(".") if mix_hidden else right.name
+            comparison = natural_compare(lname, rname, not case_sensitive)
+    elif field_name in ("extension", "Extension"):
+        lext, rext = extension_of(left.name), extension_of(right.name)
+        if not lext and not rext and left.is_hidden() != right.is_hidden():
+            comparison = 1 if left.is_hidden() else -1
+        else:
+            comparison = natural_compare(lext, rext, field_name == "extension")
+        if comparison == 0:
+            comparison = natural_compare(left.name, right.name, field_name == "extension")
+    elif field_name == "size":
+        comparison = (entry_size(left) > entry_size(right)) - (entry_size(left) < entry_size(right))
+    elif field_name in ("modified", "age", "accessed", "created", "changed"):
+        actual_field = "modified" if field_name == "age" else field_name
+        ltime = entry_timestamp_ns(left, actual_field)
+        rtime = entry_timestamp_ns(right, actual_field)
+        comparison = (ltime > rtime) - (ltime < rtime)
+        if field_name == "age":
+            comparison *= -1
+    elif field_name == "inode":
+        lino = int(getattr(left.lstat(), "st_ino", 0))
+        rino = int(getattr(right.lstat(), "st_ino", 0))
+        comparison = (lino > rino) - (lino < rino)
+    elif field_name == "type":
+        comparison = (entry_kind(left) > entry_kind(right)) - (entry_kind(left) < entry_kind(right))
+    elif field_name == "none":
+        comparison = 0
+
+    if comparison == 0 and field_name not in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name", "none"):
+        comparison = natural_compare(left.name, right.name, True)
+    return -comparison if options.reverse else comparison
+
+
+def sort_entries(entries: Iterable[Entry], options: Options) -> list[Entry]:
+    values = list(entries)
+    if options.sort_field == "none":
+        if options.reverse:
+            values.reverse()
+        return values
+    values.sort(key=cmp_to_key(lambda a, b: compare_entries(a, b, options)))
+    return values
+
+
+def visible_base(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> bool:
+    if not options.show_hidden and entry.is_hidden():
+        return False
+    if options.no_symlinks and entry.is_link():
+        return False
+    if any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(entry.name, pattern) for pattern in options.ignore_patterns):
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def display_filter(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> bool:
+    if options.only_dirs and options.only_files:
+        return entry.is_link() and options.show_symlinks
+    if entry.is_link() and options.show_symlinks:
+        return True
+    if options.only_dirs:
+        return entry.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks)
+    if options.only_files:
+        return not entry.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks) and not entry.is_link()
+    return True
+
+
+def scan_directory(directory: str, options: Options) -> tuple[list[Entry], Optional[OSError]]:
+    entries: list[Entry] = []
+    try:
+        with os.scandir(directory) as iterator:
+            for item in iterator:
+                entry = make_child(directory, item.name, options)
+                try:
+                    entry._lstat = item.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
+                except OSError:
+                    pass
+                if visible_base(entry, options):
+                    entries.append(entry)
+    except OSError as error:
+        return [], error
+    if options.show_dots and not options.tree:
+        entries.extend([
+            Entry(directory, ".", ".", synthetic=True),
+            Entry(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(directory)), "..", "..", synthetic=True),
+        ])
+    return sort_entries(entries, options), None
+
+
+def quote_name(text: str, enabled: bool) -> str:
+    return f"'{text}'" if enabled and " " in text else text
+
+
+def classify_suffix(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> str:
+    enabled = options.classify == "always" or (
+        options.classify in ("auto", "automatic") and options.stdout_tty
+    )
+    if not enabled:
+        return ""
+    if entry.is_link():
+        return "@"
+    if entry.is_dir(False):
+        return "/"
+    try:
+        mode = entry.lstat().st_mode
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+    if _stat.S_ISFIFO(mode):
+        return "|"
+    if _stat.S_ISSOCK(mode):
+        return "="
+    if os.name != "nt" and _stat.S_ISREG(mode) and mode & 0o111:
+        return "*"
+    return ""
+
+
+def render_name(entry: Entry, options: Options, override: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+    base = override if override is not None else entry.display
+    base = quote_name(base + classify_suffix(entry, options), options.quote_spaces)
+    if entry.is_link():
+        try:
+            target = os.readlink(entry.path)
+        except OSError:
+            target = None
+        if target is not None:
+            base += " -> " + quote_name(target, options.quote_spaces)
+    return base
+
+
+def format_size(number: int, style: str) -> str:
+    if style == "bytes":
+        return f"{number:,}"
+    if style == "binary":
+        base, suffixes = 1024, ("", "Ki", "Mi", "Gi", "Ti", "Pi", "Ei")
+    else:
+        base, suffixes = 1000, ("", "k", "M", "G", "T", "P", "E")
+    unit = 0
+    scale = float(number)
+    while number >= base ** (unit + 1) and unit + 1 < len(suffixes):
+        unit += 1
+        scale = number / float(base ** unit)
+    if unit == 0:
+        return f"{number:,}"
+    if scale < 10:
+        rendered = f"{scale:.1f}"
+    else:
+        rendered = f"{scale:,.0f}"
+    return rendered + suffixes[unit]
+
+
+def windows_mode(entry: Entry) -> str:
+    attrs = entry.attributes()
+    archive = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE", 0x20))
+    readonly = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY", 0x1))
+    hidden = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN", 0x2))
+    system = int(getattr(_stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM", 0x4))
+    kind = "l" if entry.is_link() else ("d" if entry.is_dir(False) else "-")
+    return "".join((
+        kind,
+        "a" if attrs & archive and kind != "d" else "-",
+        "r" if attrs & readonly else "-",
+        "h" if attrs & hidden else "-",
+        "s" if attrs & system else "-",
+    ))
+
+
+def mode_text(entry: Entry) -> str:
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        return windows_mode(entry)
+    try:
+        return _stat.filemode(entry.lstat().st_mode)
+    except OSError:
+        return "??????????"
+
+
+MONTHS = ("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")
+
+
+def datetime_for_ns(value: int) -> _datetime.datetime:
+    seconds, _ = divmod(value, 1_000_000_000)
+    return _datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(seconds, _datetime.timezone.utc).astimezone()
+
+
+def custom_time_format(moment: _datetime.datetime, pattern: str) -> str:
+    marker = "__EZA_SPACE_DAY__"
+    pattern = pattern.replace("%_d", marker)
+    try:
+        rendered = moment.strftime(pattern)
+    except (ValueError, OSError):
+        rendered = pattern
+    return rendered.replace(marker, f"{moment.day:2d}")
+
+
+def format_time(value: int, style: str) -> str:
+    moment = datetime_for_ns(value)
+    if style == "long-iso":
+        return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
+    if style == "full-iso":
+        nanos = value % 1_000_000_000
+        return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.") + f"{nanos:09d} " + moment.strftime("%z")
+    if style == "iso":
+        if moment.year == _datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().year:
+            return moment.strftime("%m-%d %H:%M")
+        return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
+    if style == "relative":
+        seconds = int((_datetime.datetime.now().astimezone() - moment).total_seconds())
+        future = seconds < 0
+        amount = abs(seconds)
+        if amount < 60:
+            return "now"
+        units = ((31_536_000, "year"), (2_592_000, "month"), (86_400, "day"),
+                 (3_600, "hour"), (60, "minute"))
+        for span, label in units:
+            if amount >= span:
+                count = amount // span
+                word = label if count == 1 else label + "s"
+                return f"in {count} {word}" if future else f"{count} {word} ago"
+    if style.startswith("+"):
+        pattern = style[1:].split("\n", 1)[0]
+        return custom_time_format(moment, pattern)
+    current_year = _datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().year
+    if moment.year == current_year:
+        return f"{moment.day:2d} {MONTHS[moment.month - 1]} {moment:%H:%M}"
+    return f"{moment.day:2d} {MONTHS[moment.month - 1]}  {moment.year:04d}"
+
+
+def long_cells(entry: Entry, options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    cells: list[str] = []
+    if not options.no_permissions:
+        cells.append(mode_text(entry))
+    if not options.no_filesize:
+        if entry.is_dir(False):
+            cells.append("-")
+        else:
+            try:
+                cells.append(format_size(int(entry.metadata(options.dereference).st_size), options.size_format))
+            except OSError:
+                cells.append("-")
+    if not options.no_time:
+        cells.append(format_time(entry_timestamp_ns(entry, options.time_field), options.time_style))
+    return cells
+
+
+def column_headers(options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    headers: list[str] = []
+    if not options.no_permissions:
+        headers.append("Mode" if os.name == "nt" else "Permissions")
+    if not options.no_filesize:
+        headers.append("Size")
+    if not options.no_time:
+        names = {"modified": "Modified", "accessed": "Accessed", "created": "Created", "changed": "Changed"}
+        headers.append("Date " + names[options.time_field])
+    return headers
+
+
+def render_long(
+    entries: Sequence[Entry], options: Options,
+    name_overrides: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
+) -> list[str]:
+    rows = [long_cells(entry, options) for entry in entries]
+    headers = column_headers(options)
+    widths: list[int] = []
+    for index in range(len(headers)):
+        values = [headers[index]] if options.header else []
+        values.extend(row[index] for row in rows)
+        widths.append(max((display_width(value) for value in values), default=0))
+
+    lines: list[str] = []
+    if options.header:
+        formatted = []
+        for index, text in enumerate(headers):
+            right = index != 0 or options.no_permissions
+            formatted.append(pad(text, widths[index], right))
+        prefix = " ".join(formatted)
+        lines.append((prefix + " " if prefix else "") + "Name")
+    for row_index, (entry, row) in enumerate(zip(entries, rows)):
+        formatted = []
+        for index, text in enumerate(row):
+            right = index != 0 or options.no_permissions
+            formatted.append(pad(text, widths[index], right))
+        prefix = " ".join(formatted)
+        override = name_overrides[row_index] if name_overrides is not None else None
+        name = render_name(entry, options, override)
+        lines.append((prefix + " " if prefix else "") + name)
+    return lines
+
+
+def render_grid(cells: Sequence[str], width: Optional[int], across: bool) -> list[str]:
+    if not cells or width is None or width <= 0:
+        return list(cells)
+    count = len(cells)
+    selected_columns = 1
+    selected_widths = [max(display_width(cell) for cell in cells)]
+    for columns in range(count, 0, -1):
+        rows = math.ceil(count / columns)
+        widths: list[int] = []
+        for column in range(columns):
+            if across:
+                indices = range(column, count, columns)
+            else:
+                start = column * rows
+                indices = range(start, min(start + rows, count))
+            values = [display_width(cells[i]) for i in indices]
+            widths.append(max(values, default=0))
+        if sum(widths) + 2 * (columns - 1) <= width:
+            selected_columns, selected_widths = columns, widths
+            break
+    rows = math.ceil(count / selected_columns)
+    lines: list[str] = []
+    for row in range(rows):
+        pieces: list[str] = []
+        for column in range(selected_columns):
+            index = row * selected_columns + column if across else column * rows + row
+            if index >= count:
+                continue
+            text = cells[index]
+            if column + 1 < selected_columns:
+                text = pad(text, selected_widths[column]) + "  "
+            pieces.append(text)
+        lines.append("".join(pieces).rstrip())
+    return lines
+
+
+def actual_width(options: Options) -> Optional[int]:
+    if options.width is not None:
+        return options.width
+    if options.stdout_tty:
+        return shutil.get_terminal_size(fallback=(80, 24)).columns
+    return None
+
+
+def render_block(entries: Sequence[Entry], options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    displayed = [entry for entry in entries if display_filter(entry, options)]
+    if options.mode == "details":
+        if options.metadata:
+            return render_long(displayed, options)
+        return [render_name(entry, options) for entry in displayed]
+    if options.mode == "grid_details":
+        detail_lines = render_long(displayed, options)
+        return render_grid(detail_lines, actual_width(options), options.across)
+    names = [render_name(entry, options) for entry in displayed]
+    if options.mode == "grid":
+        return render_grid(names, actual_width(options), options.across)
+    return names
+
+
+def os_error_number(error: OSError) -> int:
+    return int(getattr(error, "winerror", None) or getattr(error, "errno", None) or 1)
+
+
+def os_error_message(error: OSError) -> str:
+    number = os_error_number(error)
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        try:
+            message = ctypes.FormatError(number).strip()
+        except (ValueError, OSError):
+            message = ""
+    else:
+        try:
+            message = os.strerror(number)
+        except ValueError:
+            message = str(error)
+    message = message.rstrip("\r\n")
+    return f"{message} (os error {number})"
+

+@dataclass
+class DirectoryContext:
+    path: str
+    label: str
+
+
+def child_context(parent: DirectoryContext, entry: Entry) -> DirectoryContext:
+    return DirectoryContext(entry.path, os.path.join(parent.label, entry.name))

+def render_tree_root(root: Entry, options: Options, errors: list[str]) -> tuple[list[Entry], list[str]]:
+    entries: list[Entry] = [root]
+    names: list[str] = [root.display]
+
+    def descend(directory: Entry, ancestors: list[bool], depth: int) -> None:
+        if options.max_level is not None and depth >= options.max_level:
+            return
+        children, error = scan_directory(directory.path, options)
+        if error is not None:
+            errors.append(f"{directory.path}: {os_error_message(error)}")
+            return
+        visible = [child for child in children if display_filter(child, options)]
+        for index, child in enumerate(visible):
+            last = index == len(visible) - 1
+            prefix = "".join("    " if was_last else "\u2502   " for was_last in ancestors)
+            prefix += "\u2514\u2500\u2500 " if last else "\u251c\u2500\u2500 "
+            entries.append(child)
+            names.append(prefix + child.display)
+            if child.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks):
+                descend(child, ancestors + [last], depth + 1)
+
+    if root.is_dir(options.follow_symlinks):
+        descend(root, [], 0)
+    return entries, names
+
+
+def render_tree(roots: Sequence[Entry], options: Options, errors: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    all_entries: list[Entry] = []
+    all_names: list[str] = []
+    for root in roots:
+        entries, names = render_tree_root(root, options, errors)
+        all_entries.extend(entries)
+        all_names.extend(names)
+    if options.metadata:
+        return render_long(all_entries, options, all_names)
+    return [render_name(entry, options, name) for entry, name in zip(all_entries, all_names)]
+
+
+def read_input_paths(parsed: ParsedArgs, options: Options) -> list[str]:
+    if parsed.paths:
+        return list(parsed.paths)
+    stdin_tty = bool(getattr(sys.stdin, "isatty", lambda: False)())
+    if options.stdin or not stdin_tty:
+        data = sys.stdin.read()
+        separator = os.environ.get("EZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR", "\n")
+        if separator == "":
+            return [part for part in data if part]
+        return [part for part in data.split(separator) if part]
+    return ["."]
+
+
+def execute(parsed: ParsedArgs, options: Options) -> tuple[str, str, int]:
+    paths = read_input_paths(parsed, options)
+    stderr_lines: list[str] = []
+    status = 0
+    roots: list[Entry] = []
+    files: list[Entry] = []
+    directories: list[DirectoryContext] = []
+
+    for raw in paths:
+        entry = make_explicit(raw, options)
+        try:
+            entry._lstat = os.lstat(raw)
+        except OSError as error:
+            stderr_lines.append(f"{rust_debug(raw)}: {os_error_message(error)}")
+            status = 2
+            continue
+        if options.tree:
+            roots.append(entry)
+        elif entry.is_dir(False) and not options.as_file:
+            directories.append(DirectoryContext(raw, normalize_input_display(raw)))
+        else:
+            if visible_base(entry, options) and display_filter(entry, options):
+                files.append(entry)
+
+    if options.tree:
+        roots = sort_entries(roots, options)
+        lines = render_tree(roots, options, stderr_lines)
+        if stderr_lines:
+            status = 2
+        output = "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")
+        error_output = "\n".join(stderr_lines) + ("\n" if stderr_lines else "")
+        return output, error_output, status
+
+    files = sort_entries(files, options)
+    chunks: list[str] = []
+    if files:
+        chunks.append("\n".join(render_block(files, options)))
+
